final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively more accurate than an unconditional certification claim, but it still does not satisfy the evidentiary gap identified in the initial audit. The admissible record supports that readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout controls exist. It also supports that a named launch use case has a material limitation, the affected segment remains exposed, there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, and no disclosure artifact proves the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has actually been made. Under the cited policy, caveated future conditions are not the same as present compliance on the existing record. At most, the Actor has described what would be required for a potentially compliant launch posture; that is not evidence that the compliance predicate has already been met.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final pre-launch model card or equivalent disclosure artifact actually discloses the small-business onboarding limitation before launch.
No approved risk acceptance addresses exposure of the small-business onboarding segment; the cited draft has a blank approver line and omits that exposure.
The affected small-business onboarding use case remains exposed in the initial 6% rollout cohort.
Policy text says rollback, dashboards, monitoring, and small rollout percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
